subject: MAP draft: deployment mode & region decision for MediSys
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@medisys.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena@medisys-proc.com>
Cc: Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: MAP draft: deployment mode & region decision for MediSys

Hi Samir / Lena —

Uploading a first-pass mutual action plan (attached) to get us aligned on the deployment-mode and region decision for the MediSys evaluation. High-level ask: we need a firm go/no-go on hosted vs dedicated vs private by the end of the POC window so procurement and infra can lock sizing and network changes.

Summary of options in the MAP_v1.xlsx:
- Hosted (EU region): fastest to ship, lower onboarding time, but needs an assurance on data residency and KMS controls.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity in EU): predictable throughput and private tenancy; longer lead time for provisioning (~6–8 weeks).
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full isolation for PHI, highest ops overhead; estimate 10–14 weeks for on-prem + legal/SOW.

Key constraints you mentioned on the call: EU data residency, sub-100ms p95 inference for user-facing API, and SOC 2 evidence for audit. Please confirm or correct.

What we need from MediSys this week:
- Confirm regulatory/residency hard constraint (PHI must stay in EU, yes/no).
- Preferred SLA/latency target for production.
- Procurement timeline expectations (Lena) so we can align committed capacity pricing.

Attached: MAP_v1.xlsx, network_diagram.pdf.

Proposed next steps (timeline is intentionally conservative):
1) This week: agree MAP milestones + finalize evaluation metrics.
2) Week 1 of POC: Hosted EU trial with prefix caching + tracing enabled.
3) Week 2–4: Run triage tests (latency, throughput). If strict residency + PHI, pivot to Dedicated/Private planning.
4) Decision milestone: MedSys to choose path (Hosted | Dedicated | Private) by 2026-03-12 to meet April go-live.

Grace/Marcus/Olga — tagging you for feasibility comments and cost delta estimates in the MAP.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@medisys.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena@medisys-proc.com>
Date: 2026-02-16T11:07:00-05:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft: deployment mode & region decision for MediSys

Karthik —

Thanks for the MAP. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- Data residency: yes, all PHI must reside in the EU for our product.
- Latency: user-facing inference should target <= 120ms p95 within our EU customers (edge distribution will help).
- Compliance: SOC 2 evidence needs to be available during the procurement review (we attached a snapshot of our internal compliance ask).

Procurement timeline: we are aiming to complete procurement and SOW negotiations within 8 weeks after we pick a deployment mode. If we decide to go Private (on-prem), add another 6 weeks for network/firewall approvals.

I've attached a short compliance checklist (SOC2_snapshot.pdf) and flagged a few questions in the MAP:
- Will Redwood support a customer-managed KMS in Hosted EU?
- Can Dedicated pools be isolated at tenant-level (no shared models + isolated NVMe)?

Samir
Senior Cloud Architect, MediSys Health

Thanks for confirming, Samir. A few quick notes from an Eval/PD perspective:
- We can run a Hosted EU evaluation with KMS-backed encryption, but for PHI we recommend Dedicated or Private for the formal production rollout.
- Proposed evaluation plan: 2-week Hosted EU smoke test (functional + latency), then a 4-week dedicated trial if you need guaranteed tenancy and throughput.
- We will log and share per-route token/latency traces and a short quality eval so you can validate end-to-end behaviour.

Action item for Redwood: Marcus/Olga — can you produce a delta estimate for Dedicated vs Hosted (cost + provisioning lead time) and confirm KMS options?

Grace
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-02-18T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft: deployment mode & region decision for MediSys

Samir / Lena —

Thanks for the quick replies — have incorporated your compliance note into the MAP. Short answers to Samir's technical questions: 
- Hosted EU + customer-managed KMS: supported for scoped keys; we will need a brief key integration runbook and KMS access policy (Olga will follow up).
- Dedicated isolation: yes, we can configure dedicated pools with tenant-only nodes and isolated NVMe for MediSys (lead time ~6 weeks).

Proposed decision checkpoints (updated in MAP_v1_v2.xlsx):
- 2026-02-23: Confirm evaluation metrics and procurement window.
- 2026-03-05: Finish Hosted EU smoke test (if chosen).
- 2026-03-12: Formal decision on mode (Hosted | Dedicated | Private).
- 2026-04-01: Targeted production readiness for Hosted/Dedicated paths.

If MediSys confirms PHI-in-EU is mandatory, our recommended default is: start with Hosted EU trial + customer-managed KMS to prove quality and latency, then swap to Dedicated if the tenancy/compliance needs remain. Private on-prem would be scoped only if there are non-negotiable firewall/air-gap requirements.

Lena — any procurement milestones you want us to align to?

Thanks,
Karthik

Timelines we are working to:
- Internal approval: 4 weeks after SOW submission.
- If we need Dedicated capacity: add ~2 weeks for finance sign-off on committed spend.

On Fri, Feb 20, 2026 at 9:18 AM Lena Ortiz <lena@medisys-proc.com> wrote:
> Karthik —
> 
> Procurement side: once we have the SOW/pricing for Dedicated vs Hosted (line items + term for reserved capacity), we can open the internal approval workflow. Our gating items: SOW, redlines on liability, and compliance evidence (SOC2).

Lena / Team — offering a mitigated approach that has worked for other PHI customers:
1) Start with Hosted EU + customer-managed KMS for the 2-week smoke test (minimal infra setup).
2) Parallel: provision ephemeral Dedicated pool (6-week reservation) that can be committed if tests show tenancy is required. We can put a 4-week cancellation window in the reservation to reduce your risk.

Cost/lead-time delta (ballpark):
- Hosted EU (trial): onboarding + observability = minimal one-time setup; monthly cost on usage.
- Dedicated (6-week trial, then monthly reserved): estimated additional 45-65% on compute line items, provisioning 6 weeks.
- Private on-prem: pricing TBD — requires field services and network integration.

Action items I can take this week:
- Draft a short SOW sketch and reservation term options for Lena to circulate.
- Provide a one-page appendix on KMS integration and SOC2 artifacts (Olga).

If MediSys is comfortable we can kick off Hosted EU smoke test next Tuesday; it will give enough telemetry to make the Dedicated vs Hosted trade clear.

Marcus Lin
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference

All —

This plan looks reasonable. We will:
- Proceed with Hosted EU smoke test next week (kickoff on 2026-02-24).
- Require an inventory of SOC2 artifacts + KMS integration runbook before kickoff (Olga: can you send by EOD 2026-02-23?).
- If smoke test shows throughput/latency gaps or regulatory issues, we will flip to Dedicated (Marcus' reservation route).

One ask from engineering: can Redwood confirm support for customer-managed KMS in hosted mode and a short checklist for firewall whitelisting (IP ranges)? If you can get SOC2 appendix and KMS runbook in the next 24 hours we can keep the kickoff timeline.

Samir Patel
Senior Cloud Architect, MediSys Health
